To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cytotoxic effect of ATP is caused by a K+ influx, and the subsequent dissipation of the MMP.
the ATP-induced loss of viability in hepatocytes is preceded by a decrease in the mitochondrial membrane potential.
extracellular ATP induces cell death in hepatocytes, and that this is caused by an increase in intracellular K+ levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of ATP-induced hepatocyte death.
the role of intracellular Ca(2+)-induced K(+) uptake in the loss of the mitochondrial membrane potentials and cell death induced in hepatocytes by extracellular ATP.
the mechanisms of ATP-induced hepatocytotoxicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increase in [Ca(2+)](i) on exposure to ATP induces a loss in MMP and cell death.
the ATP-induced increase in [Ca(2+)]i is followed by a K(+)-mediated depolarization of the mitochondrial membrane, leading to a decrease in cellular ATP, which is followed by cell death.
the ATP-induced increase in [Ca(2+)]i is a necessary, but not sufficient condition for cell death.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ATP induces a Ca2+-dependent increase in K+ influx into hepatocytes and that a decrease in intracelluar K+ concentration protects against ATP-induced cell death.
the ATP-induced loss of viability is a consequence of the dissipation of the MMP and the resulting increase in [Ca(2+)](m).
extracellular ATP induces a loss of viability in hepatocytes by means of a mechanism which involves a Ca2+-dependent K+ influx into the mitochondria, leading to a loss of MMP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ATP-induced cell damage is mediated through the mitochondrion.

ATP-induced cell injury is a result of mitochondrial dysfunction, and that the ATP-induced mitochondrial dysfunction is a result of the increase in intracellular calcium levels and the subsequent K+ influx into the mitochondria.
ATP-induced cell killing is a consequence of a loss of MMP.
